column2:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column4: The methodology is developed to enable recurrent impact evaluations, offer recommendations for the public bodies on how to measure the impact of their own data. It uses several layers to assess impact, looking at the main publishers and re-user categories, but also using several data collection methods: user surveys, comparative analyses, portal usage, expert surveys and case studies.This will be complemented by the development of re-use impact indicators, that will be developed with the OECD as part of the project mentioned above.
column7: The Digital Government Review of Romania, conducted by the OECD and launched in December 2023 also has a dedicated chapter on Open Government Data and recommendations on Measuring the impact of open government data in Romania (https://www.oecd.org/publications/digital-government-review-of-romania-68361e0d-en.htm)

column4: (Review 1 - Answer revised). As available in the 2020-2021 Impact Study (https://data.gov.ro/pages/resources). The data gathered for the study (pages 71,77-78, 81) has revealed that the impact and use of open data within the public administration is reduced (pages 85-88) and focuses mainly on increased transparency. Furthermore, early results from the OECD Digital Government Review show the same trend. The review is under revision and due launch in October 2023.

column7: There is significant use of open data mostly by NGOs focusing on anti-corruption, public procurement, public expenditure or election data, leading to increased transparency and accountability. Such examples include https://expertforum.ro/implementare-saligny-sept2023/, vizualization and analysis of budgetary allocations from the most recent rural development program - Anghel Saligny. It uses data from the Ministry of Development, Public Works and Administration (https://data.gov.ro/dataset/plati-pni-anghel-saligny) that are regularly updated. It is important to notice that the data collection and publication has improved gradually based on constant dialogue between the ministry and reusers.

column7: There is important re-use of available health data, such as data from the Feedback Mechanism of Patients that raised awareness on existing issues: https://www.graphs.ro/feedback. The vizualization and data analysis is based on public data collected through the Patient Feedback Mechanism by the Ministry of Health, displayed on data.gov.ro and processed by Graphs.ro. The dataset is https://data.gov.ro/dataset/mecanismul-de-feed-back-al-pacientului-2023 and contains feedback data from patients that go through the national heatlh system hospitals (on cleanness, medicine availability, doctors and nurses behaviour, quality of the care/ service provided, bribes). It has garnered significant public interest by signaling systemic and specific issues in the health sector (https://www.graphs.ro/feed_presa.php)
